components.html: 03Work

narrative.overview: This is not a portfolio that shows work — it is the drawing of the work: the general-arrangement sheet an engineer produces between 'we need a system' and 'here is the system'. Every page is a plotted sheet, with a double border and registration ticks, a filing margin down the bound edge, hairline rules dividing the fields, section callouts pointing at mounted details, a schedule of parts, and a title block that closes it. The subject is a developer who architects, builds, hardens and hands over business systems alone, and the sheet is the artifact that claim naturally produces. Density is low and precision is high: nothing is decorated, everything is measured, labelled or ruled. Type is set at two extremes — a heading at drawing scale and lettering at 11px — exactly as a real sheet is lettered, and the one saturated field on any screen is the primary action. The rejected reference is the category default this world exists to refuse: a hero band over a grid of same-size project cards, with a gradient headline and a soft-shadowed card lift on hover.
keyCharacteristics: Line, label and field — never fill, shadow or ornament.
One accent, drafting redline, reserved for revision, state and the single primary action.
Two lettering registers (drawing gothic and dimension mono) with a strict division of labour.
Every claim that can be measured is drawn as a dimension, not written as an adjective.
Sheets, not pages: home is sheet 01, each case sheet 02-04, numbered on every screen.

rules.name: The One Pen Rule
rules.body: Redline is the only saturated colour, and never used for emphasis, decoration or category. It appears where a drafting pen appears: a revision, an unresolved item, the current position, and the one thing the visitor is asked to do. If a second colour seems needed, the answer is a second mark, not a second hue.

rules.name: The Cool Ground Rule
rules.body: Both grounds are blue-grey neutrals. Warm paper, cream and ivory are prohibited: the world is film and vellum, and a warm ground reads as an editorial template rather than a plotted sheet.

rules.name: The Two Registers Rule
rules.body: Mono is for what a drawing sets in mono: dimensions, codes, item numbers, domains, revision and status. Everything a person reads or clicks is the gothic. Monospace used to make something look technical is the failure this rule prevents.

rules.name: The Two Extremes Rule
rules.body: The sheet is lettered at drawing scale or at 11px, with very little between. Resist inventing a mid-size heading to soften the jump; the jump is the drawing's rhythm.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A drawing is ink on a flat sheet. Any box-shadow, bevel, emboss, glow or faux material is out of the world, including on hover. When an element needs to separate from the ground it takes a rule, a tone or a tick.

dos: Do carry state as a mark before a colour — a revision triangle, a stretched rail tick, an underline that scales in.
Do keep the filing margin empty of content at >=80rem; it belongs to the rail and the margin line.
Do give a new component a rule, a tick or a tone when it needs to separate.
Do put a fact that is not yet supplied into a redline note that names the gap, in every locale.
Do set anything a person reads or clicks in Archivo, and anything measured in Martian Mono.
Do open every field with one full-measure heavy rule and put its label in the margin at lg and above.
donts: Don't add a shadow, bevel, glow, gradient or faux material, in any theme or state.
Don't introduce a second accent colour, or use redline for anything that is not revision, state or the primary action.
Don't stack a label above a heading at any breakpoint.
Don't set body copy, headings, navigation or buttons in the mono.
Don't use a warm or cream ground; the world is film and vellum.
Don't build a grid of same-size cards; the containers are mounts, cartouches, schedules and notes.
Don't gate text on a reveal animation — content is readable at first paint, with or without JavaScript.
Don't number a section unless the sequence carries information the reader needs.
